title: CSGPolygon path mode throws errors when 2 points in curve are equal
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable, 4.3.stable, 4.1.1.stable.mono.

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads)

### Issue description

CSGPolygon throws errors when set to path mode and when 2 points in curve have equal positions.

error1:
> E 0:00:00:0274   looking_at: The target vector can't be zero.
>   <Błąd C++>     Condition "p_target.is_zero_approx()" is true. Returning: Basis()
>   <Źródło C++>   core/math/basis.cpp:1044 @ looking_at()

error2:
> E 0:00:00:0274   _find_interval: Zero length interval.
>   <Błąd C++>     Method/function failed. Returning: interval
>   <Źródło C++>   scene/resources/curve.cpp:1776 @ _find_interval()

error3:
> E 0:00:00:0274   looking_at: The transform's origin and target can't be equal.
>   <Błąd C++>     Condition "origin.is_equal_approx(p_target)" is true. Returning: Transform3D()
>   <Źródło C++>   core/math/transform_3d.cpp:82 @ looking_at()



### Steps to reproduce

 - Create Path3D
 - Create Curve3D
 - add Curve3D to path
 - Create CSGPolygon3D
 - set its mode to Path
 - set path node to Path3D
 - Create Vector3
 - add that vector more than one time to curve

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[CSGPolygon path mode throws errors when 2 points in curve are equal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20643999/CSGPolygon.path.mode.throws.errors.when.2.points.in.curve.are.equal.zip)
